interval_take:
Boxoffy this week made its first formal data science call on the ₹1,000 Cr milestone — and the answer is: D2 has not crossed it yet, and will not cross it until approximately D30 (April 17), coinciding with Bhooth Bangla's release day. Here is the model in full.

The three-layer triangulation starts with confirmed BOI data: Week 1 Hindi ₹590.36 Cr + Week 2 Hindi ₹228.97 Cr + D15–D18 confirmed (₹18.30 + ₹20 + ₹23 + ₹25) = ₹905.63 Cr Hindi nett through D18. Pinkvilla's all-India figure of ₹925 Cr through D18 implies South-dubbed has contributed just ₹19.37 Cr total — roughly ₹1 Cr/day dropping to ₹0.50 Cr by Week 3. Layer 3 applies a BOI/Sacnilk calibration ratio of 90.3% (derived from three confirmed comparison points at D16, D17, D18) to Sacnilk's confirmed D19–D21 day-wise figures, yielding ₹25.44 Cr for those three days. Total D0–D21 BOI canonical: ₹950 Cr. This also validates cleanly against our 9.5% Sacnilk inflation rule: ₹1,041 Cr × 91.4% = ₹951 Cr. Two independent approaches, ₹1 Cr apart.

The Week 4 projection (42% decay from Wk3 BOI = ₹46 Cr) has D2 ending April 15 at ₹996.6 Cr — just ₹3.4 Cr short of the milestone. D29 (Apr 16) gets to ₹998.9 Cr. D30 (Apr 17, Bhooth Bangla Day 1) tips it over: ₹1,001 Cr. BOI's own language this week — "heading towards 1,000 crore nett or very close" — is entirely consistent with a current reading of ~₹950 Cr canonical. They are not calling it done because it is not done. Sacnilk's ₹1,041 Cr figure is real — it counts all languages on their methodology — but the canonical Hindi-led BOI figure that defines the record is what matters here, and that number is ~₹950 Cr as of D21.

Sensitivity: best case (38% Wk4 decay) = D28–D29. Worst case (heavy Bhooth screen pressure) = D31–D32. Central estimate: D30, April 17. The milestone and the next big Hindi release arrive on the same day.
